slides.title: Testing new ChatGPT # prompt: write python code
slides.text: Testing new ChatGPT # prompt: write python code to generate a list # of all prime numbers between 1 and 100 def is_prime(n): """Check if a number is a prime number.""" if n <= 1: return False if n <= 3: return True if n % 2 == 0 or n % 3 == 0: return False i = 5 while i * i <= n: if n % i == 0 or n % (i + 2) == 0: return False i += 6 return True # Generate a list of prime numbers in the range 1 to 100 prime_numbers = [n for n in range(1, 101) if is_prime(n)] prime_numbers Prompt: why in your code you increment by 6 ? Response: The increment by 6 in the prime checking function is based on the observation that all primes are of the form 6k±1 (with the exception of 2 and 3) because: 6k are divisible by 6. 6k+2 are divisible by 2. 6k+3 are divisible by 3. 6k+4 are divisible by 2. That leaves only 6k+1 and 6k+5 = 6k-1 This is a common optimization for prime checking algorithms

slides.title: 01.ai - tops LLM Leaderboard https://01.ai - original
slides.text: 01.ai - tops LLM Leaderboard https://01.ai - original 6B and 34B models - open-source https://github.com/01-ai/Yi https://www.modelscope.cn/models/01ai/Yi-34B/summary The Yi series models are large language models trained from scratch by developers at 01.AI The first public release contains two bilingual (English/Chinese) base models with the parameter sizes of 6B and 34B. Both of them are trained with 4K sequence length and can be extended to 32K during inference time News 2023/11/05: The base model of Yi-6B-200K and Yi-34B-200K with 200K context length

slides.title: Trends Trend 1 - Smaller LLMs trained on
slides.text: Trends Trend 1 - Smaller LLMs trained on "traces" of bigger models Microsoft Orca - 13B open-source, trained on explanation traces of GPT-4 Open Orca Dataset - https://huggingface.co/datasets/Open-Orca/OpenOrca GPT-3 - 170B,  GPT-3-Turbo - 20B, faster, cheaper GPT-4 - 1.7T (8 models, 220B each), GPT-4-Turbo - faster, cheaper (smaller ?) Current leader of HugginFace Open LLM Leaderboard is only 34B ! New Microsoft code diffusion paper: - Diffusion-LM is only 50M, but on par with much bigger models. - suggests GPT-3.5 Turbo is only 20B https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.17680 https://www.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/comments/17jrj82/new_microsoft_codediffusion_paper_suggests_gpt35/ https://huggingface.co/papers/2310.17680 Trend 2 - teams of models/agents Microsoft AutoGen Multi-modal models New GPT-4 - text, image (understand/create), coding, browsing, etc. Trend 3 - self-checking, self-correction New GPT-4 - checks execution when writing code RAG systems - checking the data and output Trend 4 - quality of training data ( = 95% of success ) Good datasets allow to improve models' accuracy OpenAI announced Data Partnerships - to create open-source and private datasets for AI training

slides.title: HumanEval - Programming Challenges Beating GPT-4 on HumanEval
slides.text: HumanEval - Programming Challenges Beating GPT-4 on HumanEval with a Fine-Tuned CodeLlama-34B Phind-CodeLlama-34B-v2 - it's the current state-of-the-art amongst open-source models (~74% on HumanEval). https://huggingface.co/Phind/Phind-CodeLlama-34B-v2 https://www.phind.com/blog/code-llama-beats-gpt4 Note: HumanEval test is not used in Open LLM Leaderboard, on which this model is ranked very low (1098 out of ~1,600) with average score of only 37.15. HumanEval was introduced in 2021 by Open AI: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code - https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.03374 HumanEval refers to a hand-crafted dataset comprising 164 programming challenges. It is also a benchmark to evaluate LLMs. It was developed at OpenAI. https://deepgram.com/learn/humaneval-llm-benchmark HumanEval-X is a benchmark for evaluating the multilingual ability of code generative models. It consists of 820 high-quality human-crafted data samples https://paperswithcode.com/sota/code-generation-on-humaneval

slides.title: Misc Daily.AI - Publish an AI Newsletter -
slides.text: Misc Daily.AI - Publish an AI Newsletter - https://daily.ai Learning From Mistakes (LeMa) Makes LLM Better Reasoner. LeMa fine-tunes LLMs on mistake-correction data pairs generated by GPT-4 .. https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.20689v1 .. https://github.com/microsoft/CodeT First, collect inaccurate reasoning paths from various LLMs and then employ GPT-4 as a "corrector" to : (1) identify the mistake step, (2) explain the reason for the mistake, and (3) correct the mistake and generate the final answer. Autogen - https://pub.towardsai.net/autogen-is-mindblowing-4-features-that-make-autogen-the-state-of-the-art-framework-for-creating-ai-c7eb997b58a5 RAG - Picking the Best Embedding & Reranker https://blog.llamaindex.ai/boosting-rag-picking-the-best-embedding-reranker-models-42d079022e83 Reasoning over Knowledge Graphs https://ai.plainenglish.io/is-enhancing-knowledge-graphs-with-reasoning-capabilities-all-you-need-to-reason-with-llms-80eef8ff05ee The frameworks like logical rules, KG embeddings, and neural provers could be used to enhance LLMs with structured reasoning capacities. Mistral 7B: Recipes for Fine-tuning and Quantization on Your Computer https://towardsdatascience.com/mistral-7b-recipes-for-fine-tuning-and-quantization-on-your-computer-631401583f77 Advanced RAG — Improving retrieval using Hypothetical Document Embeddings(HyDE) https://medium.aiplanet.com/advanced-rag-improving-retrieval-using-hypothetical-document-embeddings-hyde-1421a8ec075a Microsoft’s Phi 1.5 small LLM (1.3 Bln params, trained on synthetic text-book data) is now "multimodal" - can view and interpret images. - https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.05463.pdf LLM - Evaluation Benchmark Cheating https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.01964.pdf https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lM8gGgiVAnQ Benchmark leakage (evaluation data is occasionally used for model training). Article presents several guidelines for both LLM developers and benchmark maintainers.

slides.title: Misc - 2 LongQLoRA : Efficient and Effective
slides.text: Misc - 2 LongQLoRA : Efficient and Effective Method to Extend Context Length of LLMs - open-source https://github.com/yangjianxin1/longqlora LongQLoRA is a memory-efficient and effective method to extend context length of LLMs with less training GPUs. On a single 32GB V100 GPU, LongQLoRA can extend the context length of LLaMA2 7B and 13B from 4096 to 8192 and even to 12k. LongQLoRA achieves competitive perplexity performance on PG19 and Proof-pile dataset after only 1000 finetuning steps, our model outperforms LongLoRA and is very close to MPT-7B-8K. Self-RAG https://levelup.gitconnected.com/upgrade-your-retrieval-augmented-generation-with-self-rag-bb30b2a0ffa4 Microsoft has over a million paying Github Copilot users "over 1 million paid copilot users in more than 37,000 organizations"

slides.title: RLHF + Reward Model + PPO on LLMs
slides.text: RLHF + Reward Model + PPO on LLMs https://medium.com/@madhur.prashant7/rlhf-reward-model-ppo-on-llms-dfc92ec3885f RLHF = Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback PPO = Proximal Policy Optimizer Reward Model We create and train the reward model using human feedback. This model then can be used instead of a human to assign different rewards to different prompt completions.

slides.title: LLMs are not good at extrapolation Pretraining Data
slides.text: LLMs are not good at extrapolation Pretraining Data Mixtures Enable Narrow Model Selection Capabilities in Transformer Models (Nov 2023, Google DeepMind) https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.00871.pdf Main idea: LLMs are not good at extrapolation . They perform well on tasks within the domain that they were trained in, but fail or significantly degrade on even simple out-of-domain extrapolation tasks. Similarity in classic ML: Can extrapolate                                   Can NOT extrapolate

slides.title: MLC LLM = Run LLMs Everywhere Machine Learning
slides.text: MLC LLM = Run LLMs Everywhere Machine Learning Compilation for Large Language Models (MLC LLM) open-source project enables deploying LLMs on a variety of hardware platforms and apps: iOS, Android, Linux, Windows, Mac, web browsers https://llm.mlc.ai https://github.com/mlc-ai/mlc-llm High-performance, native deployment of any LLM with native APIs with compiler acceleration The mission of this project is to enable everyone to develop, optimize and deploy AI models natively on everyone's devices with ML compilation techniques. For iOS - MLCChat app (iPhones and iPads) On Android - demo APK (Android Application Package) teted on Samsung and Google Pixel phones. Their C++ interface supports various GPUs across AMD, Intel, Apple, and NVIDIA, for desktop operating systems​​. A companion project, WebLLM allows the deployment of language models natively in browsers through WebGPU and WebAssembly without the need for server resources​​. They also provide resources like a GitHub repo, a web series running diffusion models in the browser, and a course for a systematic walkthrough of their approach to universal deployment​​.

slides.title: Striking Example: Albert Einstein - a Thief, a
slides.text: Striking Example: Albert Einstein - a Thief, a Liar and a Plagiarist https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/he-thief-liar-plagiarist-shimry-siddeeque/ Albert Einstein is held up as "a rare genius," who drastically changed the field of theoretical physics. The truth, however, is very different. Einstein was an inept and moronic person, who could not even tie his own shoelaces; he contributed nothing original to the science. On the contrary—he stole the ideas of others. When we actually examine the life of Albert Einstein, we find that his only 'brilliance' was in his ability to plagiarize and steal other people's ideas, passing them off as his own. This includes all his work. The special and general theories of relativity, the equivalence of energy and mass, the photon theory of light, and the explanation of Brownian motion in liquids. Everything was plagiarized. It is impossible to point the main author. Today's progress in AI is driven by tens of thousands of people from all around the globe. The truth about science is prosaic. Detailed case studies show again and again that the role of genius in advancing science is overstated. Science is the product of work of many ordinary people, just like every other human activity. Who is the "Author" of AI ?
